notes.title: Atomfall® | Can You Stop The Red Strain?
notes.content: [p][b]The Red Strain[/b], a new story expansion to Atomfall® the smash hit survival action game. A secret research site built by B.A.R.D on the site of an old missile testing facility, it has been shrouded in mystery ever since it opened. But something changed when the quarantine came into effect. [b]Now, the facility has fallen into more nefarious hands, and a deadly virus is seeping out from the secret network of underground labs and bunkers. But a route back into the facility has been located, and with it the opportunity to finally get some answers[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/40f88e606c53e2db77eda796e04673ff8ba2666d.jpg"][/img][/p][list][*][p][b]Investigate Test Site Moriah to uncover the mysteries hidden within the top-secret research facility, hidden away for years.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Find new items and upgrade unique abilities that can be used throughout the Quarantine Zone.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Enhance your arsenal with new supressed weapons and take over robot weaponry when you need some extra firepower.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Fight for survival against fearsome new foes, with some made more powerful by the Red Strain and others the result of twisted experimentation.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][i]Atomfall's® The Red Strain will launch today on [b]PC via Steam[/b].[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/16430ef95b88f8b33194d0917eda8cdb70ffe074.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]Atomfall®[/h1][p][/p][p]A UK-based post-apocalyptic survival-action game, Atomfall® is inspired by the real life Windscale nuclear incident in the 1950s. Players will embark on a fictionalised adventure meeting a cast of weird and wonderful characters as they try to uncover the mystery of what happened at the Atom Plant and escape the Quarantine Zone. So far, over 2.5 million players have jumped into the world of Atomfall®.[/p][p][/p][p]Atomfall® is available now on  [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/801800/Atomfall/"]PC via Steam[/url]. notes.title: Art thou fool or Devil? Dare you take a boat ride to Wicked Isle, available now
notes.content:
Wicked Isle, the [b]first story expansion for Atomfall®, is available now.[/b] This new pack adds the Midsummer Island location to the game together with a host of new leads, characters, enemies, weapons, items and more for you to discover. You may even uncover new potential endings for the main story.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/dae215aa6f0f2667718e7b1a5dec9d04a440054f.jpg[/img]

Included as part of the Deluxe Edition, and available for separate purchase on all platforms, Wicked Isle digs deeper into the folk horror elements of Atomfall as you take a boat ride across the dark and lonely waters of the lake in Wyndham Village to reach Midsummer Island.  

Rebellion’s Head of Design, Ben Fisher, gave us an insight into the making of Wicked Isle and what you are going to find there in our latest gameplay showcase: 

[previewyoutube=0EeNf6V-i0Q;full][/previewyoutube]

To access Wicked Isle you need to head to docks on the shore in Wyndham and find Bill Anderson, a boatman who's an expert at navigating the treacherous waters of Lake Wyndhamere. As you approach, Bill will call you over, asking for help locating something he’s lost. This is where your journey to Midsummer Isle begins. 

Once you agree to help Bill, he will take you over to the island and give you your first lead. From hereon in it is up to you to explore as you like. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/d838afcf76adc8c86e70d1f258560ef5e2c37c43.jpg[/img]

Set close to the Windscale Atom Plant and shrouded by fog, you will quickly find that the disaster has taken its toll on Midsummer Island with infection rife, affecting both the environment and those that live there. 

While you are on the island you are going to [b]meet a host of colourful new characters and enemies. A deranged druid cult has become even more powerful through their pagan rituals while roaming bandits have embraced the island’s nautical past and strange creatures lurk in the watery depths.  [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/fcfe8b18aca3708acee9952c91588acdd71a70a7.jpg[/img]

To survive you are going are going to have to make use of the new weapons and items you will find as you explore.[b] This includes a devastating Blunderbuss shotgun which inflicts huge damage but has a limited range as well as a cutlass and some strange ritualistic weapons. There is also an upgraded metal detector to find as well as a host of new skills, including Decomposition, a powerful ability that causes enemies to rapidly dissolve into fungal spores after a takedown. [/b]

There is much more for you to discover once you cross the lake to Midsummer Island, but we will leave you to explore and find them for yourselves. 

As always you can keep up to date with all the latest Atomfall news on our social channels. 

For the latest news and updates, please visit Atomfall.com and be sure to follow Atomfall® on our new social channels:[url=https://x.com/AtomfallGame] Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/AtomfallGame/]Facebook[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/atomfallgame/]Instagram[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/@RebellionGamesStudio]YouTube.[/url]

notes.title: Atomfall is getting a spooky DLC set on an offshore island that also lets you blast pretend pirates with a blunderbuss
notes.content: Atomfall wasn't as good as it could have been when it launched in March, mainly due to its barebones combat and anaemic stealth and survival systems. But I nonetheless enjoyed exploring Rebellion's eerie take on the Lake District while unravelling the mystery behind the catastrophe at the Windscale Power Plant. I'd be more than happy to ramble through a little extra of that world, and it just so happens that more Atomfall will wash up on the Cumbrian coast next week... Read more.

notes.title: Atomfall's first expansion takes you to a wicked new island when it arrives next week
notes.content:
Developer Rebellion Developments revealed a first look at Atomfall's first DLC expansion yesterday. Titled Wicked Isle, it unsurprisingly brings you to an island called Midsummer Island that is, in fact, a bit wicked, but like, in the bad way, not in the something a teen in the 2000s would say about something they like kind of way. Specifically it'll have a bit more of a folk horror vibe to it, which I'm certainly into conceptually. Lots of great folklore in the UK, as long as it's not stepping over frequently trodden upon territory.

Read more

notes.title: Atomfall® │Dare You Visit The Dark And Lonely Waters Of The Wicked Isle?
notes.content:
Something wicked this way comes... We are pleased to announce that [b]Wicked Isle[/b], a story expansion for our hit survival action title, Atomfall® will [b]launch on June 3rd[/b]. The expansion adds a [b]whole new location[/b] to the game, with its [b]own set of characters and enemies[/b] as well as [b]additional leads, weapons, skills, items and multiple new endings for the main game.[/b] 

A new trailer showcasing the content from Wicked Isle is available to watch here:
[previewyoutube=5HdforNUuuE;full][/previewyoutube]

Drawing on the [b]folk horror elements[/b] of the game for inspiration, the story expansion is [b]set on Midsummer Island[/b]. To cross to the island [b]players must talk to the boat-keeper who can be found on the jetty in Wyndham Village.[/b] He will give you information about the island as well as your first Lead.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/64f6ec1f9d49ce307331432b2d64daf4cc0922db.jpg[/img]

[i]“Midsummer is located close to the Windscale Atom Plant and as a result the levels of infection in both the people and environment are higher than on the mainland,”[/i] [b]explained Ben Fisher, Head of Design at Rebellion.[/b] [i]“You are going to meet new enemy factions including pirate bandits and infected druids. To help you survive there are new weapons to be found on the island including a devastating Blunderbuss shotgun, a new bow, cutlass, daggers and the Beekeeper’s Staff. You will also be able to acquire new skills which will aid you on your quest as well as an upgraded metal detector which will enable you find even more loot caches.”[/i]

[b]The Leads you uncover in Wicked Isle will open a variety of story threads, some of which create new potential endings for the main Atomfall® game.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/981b3a5daa8d49a417aeb1c675b0d7ce8efd6a4c.jpg[/img]

[b]Included in the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/801800/Atomfall/]Deluxe Edition[/url] and in the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3607720/Atomfall_Deluxe_Upgrade/]Deluxe Upgrade Pack[/url] and available to purchase separately when released[/b] (£14.99, €19.99, $19.99), Wicked Isle will be available from [b]June 3rd[/b] on PC via Steam.

notes.title: Rebellion's CEO says 'it looks like we want to do more Atomfall' but it will depend on whether the studio can 'find the resources to do it'
notes.content: Rebellion's open world shooter Atomfall released in March among some stiff competition, landing in the same month as Hazelight's cooperative hit Split Fiction and a week after the massively popular Assassin's Creed Shadows. Yet according to CEO Jason Kingsley, this hasn't stopped Atomfall from becoming a success in its own right. Indeed, Atomfall has done so well for Rebellion that Kingsley is considering making it into a series... Read more.

notes.title: Чаепитие на обочине: Обзор Atomfall
notes.content: Rebellion по праву считается старожилом индустрии. Основанная еще в 1993 году британская компания успела заметно вырасти в размерах и выпустить десятки разноплановых проектов, но так и не смогла пробиться в высшую лигу. Попытки предпринимались, однако результаты были весьма спорными. Особенно тяжелой выдалась вторая половина 2000-х, когда руководству пришлось закрыть офис в Дерби и перейти в консервативный режим.

notes.title: Популярность растёт: Atomfall привлекла 2 миллиона человек
notes.content: Аудитория Atomfall превысила 2 миллиона человек. Студия Rebellion опубликовала статистику шутера, отметив его большую популярность среди игроков. При этом она только растёт: в первую неделю после запуска 27 марта в постапокалиптическую Британию отправились 1,5 миллиона человек, а спустя две недели цифра выросла до 2 миллионов.

notes.title: Atomfall hits 2 million players and 500K cups of tea drunk
notes.content: Survival-action shooter Atomfall has lured more than two million players into its post-nuclear-disaster Britain, and they've apparently drunk 500,000 cups of tea while there. Which is not enough. Those are rookie numbers in the British tea drinking game. We need those numbers up to like three per person just to make average. That's 6,000,000 cups of tea, people, get on it... Read more.

notes.title: Atomfall surpasses 1.5 million players to become Rebellion's most successful game launch in 32 years
notes.content: Rebellion's been around for a long time, and it's put out a lot of videogames—some of them pretty good! But its newest release, Atomfall, may surpass them all: Rebellion says Atomfall has now surpassed 1.5 million players since its March 27 release, and now stands as the "most successful launch in the company’s 32-year history.".. Read more.

notes.title: Patch Notes | 27.03.2025
notes.content:
[h3]ATOMFALL DAY 1 UPDATE FIXES[/h3]
In addition to [b]general bug fixing and gameplay improvements[/b] the latest title update to Atomfall addresses the following issues:

[h3]Global[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed an overlapping issue in subtitles, playstyle warning messages, and barter screens 
[*] Fixed an issue where in some circumstance the AI would not escalate to combat 
[*] Fixed an issue with NPCs (such as Molly, Joyce) getting hostile with you after attacking them once and conversing continuously with them during gameplay
[*] Fixed an issue where Throwable weapons could clip through the metal barricades 
[*] Fixed an issue with Spits from ferals not generating a PFX, making it hard to see their trajectory
[*] Fixed issues where the alarm audio did not stop on exfil 
[*] Fixed an issue where multiple characters could turn hostile when the player used tools nearby
[*] Saves from different game versions are now able to be loaded
[*] Improved how AI populates when loading an autosave
[*] Player ammo and trader material counts now appear correctly after bartering
[*] Fixed an issue where the outro fails to trigger after closing the backpack opened before the end of the conversation and after selecting the escape option during gameplay
[*] Fixed a cutoff issue in tooltip bar relating to some Russian characters in the menu
[*] Fixed where item name and description could remain on screen after picking item up in Backpack 
[*] Fixed an issue where the ‘Save game time’ text appeared too long
[*] Added translations for landmines 
[*] Updated text for Field Time User Setup and Field of View slider
[/list]

[h3]Slatten Dales[/h3]
[list]
[*] Improved the effect of the torch in shadowed areas of Slatten Dales 
[/list]

[h3]Wyndham Village[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where the player failed to progress the quest 'Sims wants me question Dr Garrow' if they retrieved the information from Dr Garrow before receiving the quest
[/list]
[h3]
Casterfell Woods[/h3]
[list]
[*] Reduced character clipping through the platform while getting down from the platform near wooden logs in Casterfell Woods
[*] Improved takedown animation when crouching
[*] Fixed a collision issue on the rock present near the broken building in the Old Watermill in Casterfell Woods
[*] Updated lighting to make it easier to find Mother Jago's book in the castle
[*] Fixed progression issue when the player fails to progress through the quest on interacting with Mother Jago after picking up the Growth Serum and the book of Herbalism during the gameplay 
[*] Fixed an issue with Druids and Mother Jago appearing hostile towards the player character on entering the Castle Ruins for exfil during gameplay if you antagonised them previously
[/list]

[h3]Skethermoor[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed a crash on PS4 which occurred when players idle in Skethermore for too long 
[/list]

[h3]Interchange[/h3]
[list]
[*] Power on and power up sound in Radio Tower and Robotics Lab now fixed
[/list]

Please continue to send us your bug reports. Including screenshots, video clips and full descriptions of the issues you might encounter will be hugely beneficial. Our Player Support portal is [url=https://support.rebellion.com/hc/en-gb]here[/url].

notes.title: All Atomfall endings and how to get each one
notes.content: There are a surprising number of Atomfall endings for what is a relatively small game, but as you explore the Windscale quarantine zone, you'll find plenty of characters who are willing to help you escape. That is, if you complete a series of tasks for them, or in some cases, even sell your soul. After all, the secrets of Oberon are valuable and many hope to salvage them before shit goes sideways... Read more.

notes.title: Where to find a signal redirector in Atomfall
notes.content: ny eagle-eyed explorers will likely have noticed you need a signal redirector in Atomfall's starting bunker if you want to open those sealed doors. There's a junction just outside where you leave the scientist and upon closer examination, it says you need this particular device to interact with it. Sadly, the signal redirector requires you to progress a bit in the game first, so this is a case of coming back later... Read more.

notes.title: How to upgrade weapons in Atomfall
notes.content: Want to upgrade weapons in Atomfall? Though there's no way to improve your melee weapons beyond acquiring skills, you can buff your guns in the game, and most importantly, get rid of that horrible rust coating every single one of them—there's nothing more satisfying than blasting some filthy outlaw with your pristine Webley revolver... Read more.

notes.title: Should you report Morris Wick in Atomfall?
notes.content: So you've discovered Morris Wick's crime in Atomfall, but you're unsure whether to report him to the authorities or agree to keep his secret. If you happened upon the murder of Maisie in St. Katherine's church and investigated Wyndham Village, you likely found the brewery cellar and the letter contained within that implicates Morris in the crime... Read more.

notes.title: Should you free Doctor Garrow in Atomfall?
notes.content: Deciding whether to free Doctor Garrow in Atomfall is a bit of a headscratcher. On one hand, this scientist says she can help you escape the zone and provide some answers about what the hell's going on. On the other hand, though, Captain Sims sent you to interrogate the rogue researcher and will, understandably, be a bit miffed if you up and decide to let her go... Read more.

notes.title: Where to find June's key in Atomfall
notes.content: Trying to find June's key to open her lockbox in Atomfall takes a bit of exploration. June was the owner of the Little Tea Room, but since this isn't actually one of the marked locations in Wyndham Village, it's understandable you'd be left scratching your head about where to obtain it. Below I'll explain where exactly to find June's key... Read more.

notes.title: Should you choose GEN ERA or GEN MOVE in Atomfall?
notes.content: Deciding whether to side with Joyce Tanner or Dr. Garrow in Atomfall is a tough decision. Though Garrow's past is murky at best, she was one of the leading scientists in charge of the Oberon project and so has a lot left to tell you. Joyce Tanner, by comparison, doesn't seem to know all that much, but she does promise you a way out that doesn't involve consorting with someone who might be a war criminal... Read more.

notes.title: Where to find the church cellar key in Atomfall
notes.content: If you're looking for the church cellar key in Atomfall, you're in for a lot more than you bargained. You were probably thinking this key was just tucked away in St. Katherine's church somewhere and that you could quickly grab it for some cheeky looting. Alas, it requires a fair bit of progress into the Interchange before you can grab the church cellar key... Read more.

notes.title: Atomfall hidden cache locations
notes.content: Finding hidden cache locations in Atomfall is a great way of getting spare crafting resources, items, and recipes, though you'll need a metal detector first. There are a few places you can get one; barter for it with Reg in the Slate Mine Caves, grab one for free near the radio tower in Slatten Vale, or even filch a free one from a scientist's corpse at Brinsop Manor in Skethermoor... Read more.

notes.title: Atomic battery locations in Atomfall
notes.content: Finding atomic battery locations in Atomfall is one of the key progressions in the game, as you power up the quarantined facilities of the Interchange and open the way to Oberon. These nuclear power sources are quite rare and there are only a limited number scattered around the map, generally at the end of enemy-infested areas... Read more.

notes.title: 7 things to find first in Atomfall
notes.content: Knowing what to find first in Atomfall can be a little tricky. Though the rolling hills of Cumbria are less expansive than Fallout's post-apocalyptic wastelands, there are still different routes to take as well as secret bunkers and caves to explore. You're more than welcome to wander off into the countryside and take things as they come—that's often the most fun approach... Read more.

notes.title: Atomfall (Xbox Series X) Review
notes.content:
It has been over 30 years since Rebellion opened its doors and delivered its debut title, Lords of the Realm. Since then, the developer has been known to launch titles in the fan-favourite Sniper Elite series, with a staggering 10 total titles under their belt in the series to date. Atomfall is not just a foray into a brand-new world in gaming; it’s unexplored territory for a developer with ‘veteran’ on their resume. Atomfall delivers a stunning new world saturated in gorgeous visuals developed with Rebellions i-house Asura Engine, another sandbox title to explore, and many elements other open-world titles are known for (including novel ideas from the brains at Rebellion) wrapped in a neat package.

Five years have passed since the real-life Windscale Disaster ravaged Northern England in 1957. In Atomfall, this disaster was fictionalized as worse than the real-world twin (although the ‘real’ disaster was considered the worst in English history) to the point of a large quarantine... Read more

notes.title: Atomfall review
notes.content: I've spent years wandering many an inhospitable wasteland, so Atomfall's pleasant post-apocalypse is pretty inviting. They've got tea here. And bakeries. And it's extremely green—not because of radiation storms, but because it's all pastures and woods and verdant hills as far as the eye can see. It'd be a nice place for a ramble, if it weren't for the fire-spewing robots, lethal flora, bandits, cultists and conspiracies... Read more.

notes.title: Rebellion CEO seems kind of awed by major studios making massive videogames: 'How do you organize a game that has 2,000 people working on it?'
notes.content: During a recent, wide-ranging interview with PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens, Rebellion CEO Jason Kingsley said the studio's formula for success is built on being "very professional with controlling scope and costs," and a willingness to say, when necessary, "guys, this game's too big." But while making massive, sprawling games isn't something Kingsley seems interested in doing, he does seem genuinely impressed by those who do it... Read more.

notes.title: Rebellion CEO puts the studio's recent avoidance of layoffs down to control of scope and cost: 'Sometimes we say, guys, this game's too big'
notes.content: PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens recently spoke to Rebellion CEO Jason Kingsley about the studio's extremely British survival FPS Atomfall, which is a kind of Fallout: It's Grim Up North Edition. (Or possibly Stalker: Shadow of Cumbria.) During that conversation, Josh asked how the studio had managed to avoid the layoffageddon that's hit the rest of the games industry following the Covid boom... Read more.

notes.title: As a Stalker sicko, the 2 hours I just spent with Atomfall have made it one of my most-anticipated games this year
notes.content: For over a decade, Atomfall has been Rebellion CEO Jason Kingsley's "dream game," one he was dropping coy, detail-free allusions to in chats with PCG all the way back in 2018... Read more.

notes.title: Atomfall Hands-On Preview – It’s Like Sniper Elite, But…
notes.content:
When Rebellion Developments announced Atomfall, I was intrigued. I love the Sniper Elite series, and I was excited to see the studio stretch its legs after making nothing but Sniper Elite games since around 2013. An RPG-esque Fallout-style game set in the 1960s after a nuclear disaster turns England into a post-apocalyptic, radioactive quarantine zone? That premise alone had me hooked. Imagining that setting mixed with the incredible mechanics that Rebellion is known for? What could go wrong?

Well, after just over an hour with Atomfall, I have some concerns.

As I mentioned, Atomfall follows the protagonist—an amnesiac with no identity—who must explore a quarantine zone in the Lake District, Northern England, five years after the Windscale nuclear disaster to uncover the truth about what happened. The world is full of doomsday cultists, rogue military factions, robots, radioactive monstrosities, and, of course, bandits. Lots and lots of bandits.

The story elements I... Read more

notes.title: Atomfall is basically British Fallout with a metal detector, and that'll do me chuck
notes.content: Featured in the PC Gaming Show's Most Wanted with new gameplay footage, Rebellion's Atomfall is essentially out to answer the question "What if Stalker, but in 1960s Britain?" The game is an alt-history that takes as its foundation the Windscale fire of 1957, the biggest nuclear disaster in UK history, which saw three days of fire and radioactive fallout spreading across the UK and Europe. At the time the UK government covered-up just how bad things had gotten: In Atomfall, the area around the disaster is quarantined, and things get even worse... Read more.

notes.title: Atomfall | Coming March 2025
notes.content:
[h1]The Mystery of Windscale [/h1]

Atomfallers, 

Didn't make it to cologne for Gamescom 2024? Don't worry, we've got you covered. 

Delve deeper into the foreboding world of Atomfall and the mystery of Windscale by watching the new trailer, unveiled at this year's Gamescom. 

[previewyoutube=-ni32Aw4p70;full][/previewyoutube]
Opening in the style of a classic 1950s news reel, this latest trailer offers a closer look at Atomfall’s setting in the North of England. Atomfall is inspired by the real-life events of the 1957 Windscale disaster and the story picks up five years later in a fictionalised quarantine zone that encompasses rolling countryside, valleys, caves and even a picturesque English village. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/5bc1cfd69d79f452126715f216e9b9332107fdf4.jpg[/img]
But this picture-perfect postcard setting is a hostile landscape that hides a dark mystery. To get to the bottom of what happened at Windscale, you will need to navigate military encampments, delve through abandoned bunkers below ground, and risk your life in Pagan ruins. Your trusty metal detector will also help you uncover a few secrets buried beneath the surface! 

Central to the dark mystery are the host of eccentric characters and cryptic organisations that inhabit the quarantine zone. These individuals have been cut off from the outside world for years and left to their own devices, so are anything but normal. Your interactions with them are important and will shape your journey. But be careful, they aren’t all friendly and you will need to get to grips with an array of ranged and melee weapons if you are to survive!

We're beyond excited to show you more about this brand new title in the coming months so stay tuned and, as always...observe protocol.

notes.content:
Take a sneak peak of what’s to come in this mysterious and unsettling world with [b]Atomfall’s reveal trailer.[/b]

https://youtu.be/YVodeYXYKt4

Announced at the Xbox Games Showcase Atomfall will be a day one release on [b]Xbox Game Pass[/b] and will launch simultaneously on [b]Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Windows PC, PC via Steam and Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 4 in 2025.[/b]
Atomfall is a new single player survival-action game set in post-war Britain, with players exploring a mysterious nuclear quarantine zone in the North of England.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/3eeeb29374acaabd6f55689a6dffeb38b2efefd5.png[/img]

Inspired by the real-life events of the 1957 Windscale disaster in the North of England, you pick up the story five years after the fire in a fictionalised quarantine zone. A lot has changed in this time and you’ll need to explore this hostile world and navigate bizarre characters, mysticism, cults and murky government agencies. 

Defend yourself with a selection of weapons (including pistols, SMGs, bows and arrows and more) and if that’s not your style, feel free to give your enemies a whack with a cricket bat.  
Supplies are scarce in Atomfall. You will need to hunt and scavenge for resources including food, crafting materials, weapons and ammunition. Your metal detector will help you scavenge and unearth other secrets too… 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/2572f39973077a227644b3cb0aaef1a1ce42057e.png[/img]

In response to the disaster, the army has been sent in to create and maintain a quarantine zone. This response force is known as ‘Protocol’. They are the ones tasked with keeping people safe -but after five years, their outlook has soured. 

You will learn more about Protocol as you interact with them - and the people they seek to control – over the course of the game. Are they a force for good, keeping people safe? Are they a force of oppression, making life harder for those in the quarantine zone? Or is there more going on than meets the eye?

Protocol are using all the resources at their disposal to maintain the quarantine. This includes scavenging equipment from B.A.R.D. (British Atomic Research Division) science bunkers. The robots are programmed to do everything necessary to maintain the quarantine. You need to make sure you know what you are doing before choosing to take one on. We hope you weren’t expecting a pleasant quiet walk in the country! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057216/4967e5fcc8341dcd510b1af922ab8538a877cc03.png[/img]
